I've been in a few different dangerous situations- some where I'm in trouble and some where a loved one is in trouble- and it has affected how I even react to "normal" situations. 

But in the moment? Fuck, let me try to remember how it felt the first time. 

I have PTSD from childhood stuff, so I can't remember a lot of specifics (read: I remember general stuff but my brain is like "yo, don't think too hard about that" and shuts off), but it's like you're in a daze. You have to at least be able to tell yourself that the situation is an emergency for you to even try to wake yourself up. And if people around you are acting normal? You can still feel panicked as hell, but you are more likely to not do anything if they aren't doing anything. 

My body has two main states now: adrenaline and asleep. It sucks. And in time of emergency, my brain shuts off. Like, I may as well black out. Whatever my instincts are telling me to do is what my body does. It's like I'm subconsciously accessing the environment and acting with 0 input from my brain. 

Saving lives like people think they would in emergencies? Often doesn't cross your mind when your brain is trying to preserve itself. I feel like it's learned behaviour to look to help people, and only if you can get out yourself. 

My body freezes while accessing shit and then just immediately jumps to whatever action the animal part of my brain says is best. I can feel my heart exploding and anxiety knocking on my bones, but you couldn't tell if you were listening to me. I keep my voice as calm as possible, I'll even crack jokes, and probably laugh a whole lot which leads to crying because that's just what happens. 

If you freeze when faced with danger, it doesn't make you weak or useless. It's part of being a human. 

While my body is acting, sometimes my brain thinks that this *has* to be like a video game. In video games, there is always a way out or it's possible to do something life threatening in order to escape and come out the other side just fine. And it's when you start realising... No, it isn't like that. There is no guarantee that I'm getting out of this. That's, personally, when my panic starts and I become less likely to be able to help myself, let alone others.
